misconception_description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must be explicitly compared to True or False to be used in conditionals.

solutions.generated_code:
program SaringKataPanjang
kamus
  n, m, i, panjangKata : integer
  kata : string
algoritma
  input(n, m)
  for i <- 1 to m do
    input(kata)
    panjangKata <- panjang(kata)
    if (panjangKata > n) == true then
      output(kata)
    endif
  endfor
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student added an explicit comparison to True in the conditional statement (len(x) > n) == True. The student believes that conditional expressions must be explicitly compared to True or False to be used in if statements. While this is redundant and poor style, it doesn't affect the correctness of the program - the code will still function properly and return the correct results. The student is confident this is the proper way to write conditionals in Python.
